questions.question: Where should a question's supporting detail go?

options.label: Above the question (Recommended)
options.description: Background and evidence first, then the question last, right before the options. Matches the one instance that actually read well today, and needs no extra round trip. Cost: unbounded background still pushes the question down the screen, so a long one recreates the burying problem the limit was meant to fix — which means the detail can't truly be unbounded after all.

options.label: A one-line pointer, detail on request
options.description: The question says the evidence exists and offers it; you ask if you want it. Keeps the question genuinely short and the detail genuinely unbounded. Cost: an extra round trip exactly when you do want the evidence, and if you don't ask, evidence that would have changed your answer is never seen.

options.label: Write it to a file and link it
options.description: Detail goes to a scratch file, the question carries the path. Unbounded, never in the way, and survives the conversation. Cost: leaves the conversation to read it — more friction than scrolling, and a file nobody opens is the same as no evidence.
